cities.name: Srinagar
cities.overview: The summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, set around Dal Lake with Mughal gardens, houseboats and old wooden mosques.
cities.history: Said to date from Ashoka's reign, it grew into a great centre of Kashmiri learning and craft. The Mughals loved it, and they laid out terraced gardens along Dal Lake from the early 17th century.

cities.name: Gulmarg
cities.overview: A high meadow resort at about 2,650 m in Baramulla district, India's leading ski destination in winter.

cities.name: Katra
cities.overview: A town in Reasi district at the foot of the Trikuta hills, base camp for the pilgrimage to Vaishno Devi.

cities.name: Jammu
cities.overview: The winter capital of the union territory, a city of temples at the foot of the hills.
cities.history: The seat of the Dogra rulers, who took Kashmir under the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846 and ruled the combined state until 1947.

cities.name: Pahalgam
cities.overview: A valley town on the Lidder River, a base for treks and the Amarnath pilgrimage.

cities.name: Sonamarg
cities.overview: The Meadow of Gold, a high valley on the road to Ladakh.

cities.name: Anantnag
cities.overview: A district town in south Kashmir, close to Martand and the springs of Verinag.

cities.name: Bandipora
cities.overview: A northern town on the shore of Wular Lake.

cities.name: Budgam
cities.overview: A district just south of Srinagar, gateway to the meadows of Doodhpathri.

cities.name: Udhampur
cities.overview: A town on the Jammu to Srinagar road, close to Patnitop.

cities.name: Doda
cities.overview: A hilly district in the Chenab valley, known for Bhaderwah.

places.name: Dal Lake
places.shortDescription: Srinagar's mirror-calm lake of shikaras, carved-wood houseboats, floating gardens and Mughal gardens on its shore.
places.description: Dal Lake is the heart of Srinagar. Gliding across it in a shikara at dawn reveals floating vegetable markets, lotus beds and kingfishers, while evening rides catch sunsets over the Zabarwan hills. Staying a night on one of the ornate cedar-wood houseboats is a classic Kashmir experience. The Mughal gardens of Nishat Bagh and Shalimar Bagh line the eastern shore, and the Char Chinar island sits in the middle of the lake.
places.history: The Mughal emperors made Kashmir their summer retreat and laid out the terraced gardens along Dal Lake in the 17th century. Houseboats became popular in the British era, when outsiders were not permitted to own land.
places.bestTimeNote: April to June and September to October. Tulip season at the nearby Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden is late March to April.

entryFee.note: Shikara rides at government-fixed hourly rates.

location.address: Dal Lake, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir 190001

places.name: Gulmarg
places.shortDescription: A flower-filled meadow in summer and India's top ski slope in winter, served by one of the world's highest cable cars.
places.description: Gulmarg, 'meadow of flowers', is a bowl of grassland ringed by pine forest in the Pir Panjal range. The two-stage Gulmarg Gondola climbs from the resort to Kongdoori and then to near Apharwat peak at about 3,950 m, giving access to some of Asia's best powder skiing from December to March. In summer the meadows are carpeted with wildflowers and popular for pony rides, golf and treks to Alpather Lake. Book gondola tickets online in advance.
places.history: The British developed Gulmarg as a hill resort in the late 19th century, building a golf course that is among the highest in the world. The gondola opened its first phase in 1998.
places.bestTimeNote: December to March for skiing; May to June and September to October for meadows and treks.

entryFee.note: Gondola tickets priced by phase; book on the official cable car website.

location.address: Gulmarg, Baramulla district, Jammu and Kashmir 193403

places.name: Vaishno Devi Temple
places.shortDescription: A cave shrine of the mother goddess in the Trikuta hills, reached by a 12 km uphill pilgrimage from Katra.
places.description: Mata Vaishno Devi is worshipped in a holy cave in the Trikuta hills in the form of three natural rock formations, or pindis. Millions of pilgrims make the yatra each year, walking a well-maintained path of about 12 km from Katra, or using ponies, battery cars and helicopters for parts of the route. Registration is mandatory and done online or at Katra, and each pilgrim receives an RFID card. Many continue to the Bhairon Nath temple higher up, now linked by a ropeway.
places.history: The shrine is one of the most visited in India. The Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board has managed it since 1986.
places.bestTimeNote: March to June and September to October. Navratri is especially busy; winter brings snow on the upper path.

entryFee.note: Free darshan; yatra registration is mandatory.

location.address: Trikuta Hills, Katra, Reasi district, Jammu and Kashmir 182301

places.name: Shalimar Bagh
places.shortDescription: The grandest Mughal garden in Kashmir, built by Jahangir for Nur Jahan, north-east of Dal Lake.
places.description: Terraces, water channels and black marble pavilions lie under huge chinar trees. Autumn colours make it especially beautiful.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Nishat Bagh
places.shortDescription: The Garden of Bliss, a terraced Mughal garden on the eastern bank of Dal Lake.
places.description: Twelve terraces climb the hill above the lake, with views of the Pir Panjal range. It's the largest of the Mughal gardens in Kashmir.
places.history: Designed by Asif Khan, brother of Nur Jahan, in 1633.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Chashme Shahi
places.shortDescription: A small Mughal garden from 1632, built around a mountain spring above Dal Lake.
places.description: The smallest and among the most charming of the Mughal gardens. People still come to fill bottles from the spring.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Pari Mahal
places.shortDescription: A seven-terraced Mughal garden on the Zabarwan range, with arches overlooking Dal Lake.
places.description: The Palace of Fairies was built by Dara Shikoh as a school of astrology. Its terraces and arches overlook the whole city, especially at dusk.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

images.credit: Basharat Alam Shah from Chicago, USA

places.name: Hazratbal Shrine
places.shortDescription: A white-domed shrine on Dal Lake, which holds a relic believed to be a hair of the Prophet Muhammad.
places.description: A gleaming marble mosque on the northern shore of the lake, a major pilgrim site for Kashmiri Muslims, with the relic displayed on special days.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Jamia Masjid, Srinagar
places.shortDescription: A huge old mosque in Srinagar, held up by hundreds of pillars of deodar wood.
places.description: A big courtyard with four pagoda-like towers, in a design that's unique to Kashmir. Each wooden pillar is made from one deodar trunk.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Shankaracharya Temple
places.shortDescription: A hilltop Shiva temple on the Zabarwan range, overlooking Dal Lake and all of Srinagar.
places.description: A long flight of stone steps leads up to an old stone temple on a hill. Visitors leave phones behind at security, and the view is the best in the city.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Dachigam National Park
places.shortDescription: A national park 22 km from Srinagar and the last home of the Kashmir stag, or hangul.
places.description: Forest, meadows and streams reach up from just outside the city, with black bears and rare hangul. Permits are needed.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Doodhpathri
places.shortDescription: A green meadow valley in Budgam, an easy day trip from Srinagar, with streams and pine forest.
places.description: Name means Valley of Milk, after the white rushing stream. It's quieter than Gulmarg and Pahalgam, with horses and picnickers.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Betaab Valley
places.shortDescription: A green valley 15 km from Pahalgam, named after a Bollywood film shot here.
places.description: A walled park of meadows and a clear stream, with snowy peaks behind. It's an easy stop on the road to Chandanwari.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Aru Valley
places.shortDescription: A village and meadow at the top of a side valley, 12 km from Pahalgam, and a base for treks.
places.description: A peaceful meadow village, starting point of the treks to Kolahoi Glacier and Tarsar Lake.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Amarnath Cave
places.shortDescription: A high Himalayan cave with an ice lingam of Shiva, reached on a hard annual pilgrimage.
places.description: Thousands walk or ride to this cave at about 3,888 m during the summer yatra. Registration is mandatory.
places.bestTimeNote: The yatra runs only for a short window each summer, and requires advance registration and a health certificate.

places.name: Martand Sun Temple
places.shortDescription: The grand ruins of an 8th-century sun temple on a plateau in south Kashmir.
places.description: Huge blocks of grey limestone, with a colonnaded courtyard, on a plateau with views across the valley. It's among the finest ruins in Kashmir.
places.history: Built by King Lalitaditya of the Karkota dynasty in the 8th century.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Wular Lake
places.shortDescription: One of Asia's largest freshwater lakes, in north Kashmir near Bandipora.
places.description: A wide, shallow lake fed by the Jhelum, with reeds, fishermen and mountains. The sunset is memorable.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Thajiwas Glacier
places.shortDescription: A short pony ride or walk from Sonamarg to a glacier that holds snow all summer.
places.description: The classic Sonamarg outing, with a walk or pony ride up a side valley to a patch of year-round snow. It's also a starting point for treks.
places.bestTimeNote: Security conditions and access to some spots in Kashmir can change at short notice, so check before you travel.

places.name: Raghunath Temple
places.shortDescription: A big temple complex in the old city of Jammu, one of the largest in north India.
places.description: Seven shrines with gold-coloured spires, and thousands of salagrams inside. It was begun by Maharaja Gulab Singh.
places.history: Begun in 1835 by Gulab Singh and finished by his son Ranbir Singh.

places.name: Bahu Fort
places.shortDescription: A fort above the Tawi River in Jammu, with a Kali temple and a large terraced garden.
places.description: A very old fort that has a popular temple inside it, the Bawe Wali Mata. The Bagh-e-Bahu garden beside it overlooks the river.

places.name: Mubarak Mandi Palace
places.shortDescription: The old Dogra palace complex in Jammu, a mix of Rajasthani, Mughal and European styles.
places.description: A large crumbling complex, with the Dogra Art Museum in the Pink Hall. Restoration work is under way.

places.name: Mansar Lake
places.shortDescription: A wooded hill lake 60 km from Jammu, with old temples and a walking path around it.
places.description: A calm lake surrounded by forest, with old shrines to the serpent god Sheshnag. Boats and a path around the shore are popular.

places.name: Patnitop
places.shortDescription: A hill resort at about 2,000 m on the road to Srinagar, with pine forest and winter snow.
places.description: A popular stop on the old highway, with paragliding, forest walks and Nag Temple. Snow arrives in winter.

places.name: Bhaderwah
places.shortDescription: A green valley in Doda, sometimes called Mini Kashmir, with meadows and a historic town.
places.description: Forested hills and the meadows of Padri, on a route to Chamba. It's far off the usual tourist trail.
